recentItems.description:
In this VladTV sit-down, DJ Vlad appears on camera for a wide-ranging interview with Mike Tyson that moves from boxing history to a tense exchange over Tyson’s relationships with figures from his past. Tyson reflects on reports of earning $300 million, bankruptcy, survivor’s remorse, and giving away luxury cars, while Ed Lover’s legendary Bentley story resurfaces. The conversation also covers Larry Holmes, Don King’s cash offers, Rocky Marciano, Joe Frazier, Evander Holyfield, Buster Douglas, and the Don King lawsuit.

Tyson opens up about fame, self-hate, media scrutiny, Tupac’s publicity mindset, TK Kirkland, his wife’s influence, Mike Tyson’s Mysteries, Broadway, podcasts, Queens, New York, Vegas, Jersey, and Macau. Vlad also asks about Zip, Puffy, and Southside Crips connections, prompting one of the interview’s sharpest moments.

Memo600 sits down with VladTV to reflect on his years with Lil Durk’s OTF, explaining why he didn’t release more music despite early buzz, big views, and hit records. The Chicago rapper opens up about immaturity, lack of self-belief, and chasing fame before taking rap seriously.

The conversation also revisits King Von’s rise after prison, his close bond with Durk, and the role of Track’s management as Von became one of the biggest names in drill music. Memo details how the legal situation surrounding Von and Durk kept them apart physically, even as their music connected with fans worldwide.

In a candid moment, Memo recalls Von calling him emotional over the shooting case, worried about returning to prison while major money and opportunity were finally on the table.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/AxHbPY_r1q4
--------
In this VladTV interview, Carlos Lehder revisits his rise from working with Boston George, George Jung, to building one of the biggest cocaine smuggling routes of the early 1980s. Lehder details how their partnership ended in Florida, his move to Los Angeles for new connections, and his eventual return to the Bahamas, where he acquired Norman’s Cay as a private island hub for trafficking cocaine into Florida. He discusses the operation’s reported $300 million-a-year scale, the role of planes, boats, lawyers, workers, and bribes, and how Colombian suppliers—including Pablo Escobar and other Medellín Cartel figures—relied on him to move product into the United States. Lehder also reflects on the consequences, calling his choices a tragic mistake and warning younger generations about the human cost of drug trafficking after serving 33 years in federal prison.

--------
Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev sits down with DJ Vlad to address AMC CEO Adam Aron’s criticism of Robinhood’s stock tokens, including Aron’s claim that the product is “disgusting,” a fake market, and should face SEC scrutiny. Tenev explains why Robinhood launched tokenized U.S. stocks in Europe, how the system works for investors outside the United States, and why he believes it can expand access to American capital markets in more than 120 countries.

The conversation breaks down voting rights, custody, arbitrage, DeFi, stablecoin-style backing, ADR comparisons, and whether AMC benefits from a new global pool of buyers. Tenev also discusses Robinhood Chain, real-world asset tokenization, NFTs, Bitcoin products like IBIT, fractional ownership of art such as Basquiat, and future possibilities involving private companies. A sharp look at crypto, stock market innovation, regulation, and the ongoing tension between Robinhood and the AMC “apes” community.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Harlem rapper G. Dep reflects on his teenage years, early exposure to guns, and the realities of street life before his music career. Speaking with Vlad, he explains why he avoided carrying firearms while hustling, noting that police searches were common and that carrying a gun meant risking serious charges. G. Dep also describes how drugs were hidden during encounters with police, offering a blunt look at the survival tactics used on the block.

The conversation moves through his time in high school, a brief stint at a college in New Rochelle, and his return to his grandmother’s neighborhood after leaving school. G. Dep recalls moving between his mother’s home in New Jersey and the Johnson area, saying that returning to his grandmother’s place felt less like punishment and more like going back to what he already knew.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/W6Vqal8IQfk
--------
William Noguera sits down with Vlad to recount the moment he was sentenced to death at 23 and transferred to San Quentin, where he became one of California’s youngest condemned prisoners after Proposition 7 and the Briggs Initiative era. Noguera describes arriving on death row, time in the Adjustment Center, and the racial politics that shaped daily life inside the prison system.

He also recalls living just three cells away from Stanley “Tookie” Williams, the Crips co-founder, describing him as intelligent, soft-spoken and physically imposing. The conversation also covers high-profile inmates at San Quentin, including Richard Ramirez, the “Night Stalker,” and what Noguera says happened when Ramirez entered the yard. From prison hierarchy to infamous serial killers like Lawrence Bittaker, Rodney Alcala and others, Noguera offers a firsthand look at survival, reputation and violence on California’s death row.
